title: Zeeman spin quantum geometry and intrinsic gyrotropic spin current
abstract: We uncover an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) driven solely by an oscillating magnetic field, arising from the spin version of Zeeman quantum geometry. Using the density matrix formalism, we derive the IGSC in the low-frequency clean limit, in terms of the Zeeman spin quantum metric and the Zeeman spin Berry curvature. The effect is studied in a minimal Rashba-Dresselhaus model that also supports intrinsic gyrotropic charge currents from the Zeeman Berry curvature. The spin and charge currents exhibit a $π/2$ phase shift and are found to be perpendicular to each other for certain parameter ranges. This not only enables spin current detection but also opens pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics. We further observe that these currents switch directions between longitudinal and transverse relative to the applied field, depending on the relative strength of Rashba and Dresselhaus interactions.
summary: This work theoretically derives an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) in a 2DEG model subjected to an oscillating magnetic field. The effect arises from the spin geometry (Zeeman quantum geometry) and is analyzed using the density matrix formalism. The key finding is that the spin and charge currents are perpendicular, opening pathways for pure spin current spintronics.
main_problem: The paper uncovers an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) driven solely by an oscillating magnetic field, originating from the spin version of Zeeman quantum geometry.
main_result: The spin and charge currents are found to be perpendicular for certain parameter ranges, and the IGSC can open pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics.
method: The IGSC is derived using the density matrix formalism, employing the Zeeman spin quantum metric and the Zeeman spin Berry curvature in the low-frequency clean limit.
model_or_system: The study uses a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) model incorporating Rashba and Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling (SOC) and subjected to an oscillating magnetic field.
key_observables: Intrinsic Gyrotropic Spin Current (IGSC), local spin conductivity components (Z_z^{\pm}), and the relative phase shift ($\pi/2$) between spin and charge currents.
important_parameters: The relative strengths of Rashba ($\alpha$) and Dresselhaus ($ eta$) SOC interactions, and the chemical potential ($\mu$) regime ($\mu > 0$ vs $\mu < 0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in the low-frequency clean limit, and approximations are made regarding the energy scales ($\hbar\omega \ll \epsilon_{mn}$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows the energy dispersion relation; Figure 2 illustrates the k-space distribution of the local intrinsic gyrotropic components; Figure 3 plots the amplitude of the IGSC versus the chemical potential $\mu$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically derives the IGSC using the density matrix formalism, analyzes its dependence on SOC parameters ($\alpha,  eta$) and chemical potential ($\mu$), and compares the resulting spin and charge current behaviors.
why_interesting: The explicit derivation of spin currents from geometric properties (Berry curvature/metric) in a clean limit framework provides a powerful theoretical tool applicable to understanding spin transport in condensed matter systems, which is relevant to open quantum systems dynamics.

Spintronics.note: The new paper directly derives an intrinsic gyrotropic spin current (IGSC) and discusses opening pure spin current channels for energy-efficient spintronics in a 2DEG model, which is highly relevant to the spintronics theme.
